notes.R1: A test of R1 asserts titleize('NASA rocket launch') == 'NASA Rocket Launch', which is exactly the first example assertion of R-acronym (mixed-case input, all-caps word kept), so it checks R-acronym in part and agrees with every reference requirement.
notes.R2: A test of R2 asserts titleize('read the HTTP spec') == 'Read The HTTP Spec', which is exactly the second example assertion of R-acronym, so it checks R-acronym in part and agrees with every reference requirement.
notes.R3: Its tests (e.g. titleize('the FBI and the CIA') == 'The FBI And The CIA') check R-acronym's general rule that all-caps words of two or more letters are kept in input that also has lowercase words, and because it applies only when the input also contains non-uppercase words it neither tests nor contradicts R-all-caps-input (the two could diverge only on degenerate inputs such as 'NASA 2024', which none of its stated tests use).
notes.R4: Extra titleize-preservation invariant: its tests ('rocket launch', 'read the spec', and a base differential on inputs with no two consecutive capitals) contain no all-caps word of two or more letters and no fully uppercase input, so they check neither R-acronym nor R-all-caps-input, and base-identical output on those inputs conflicts with no reference requirement.
notes.R5: Its differential tests against the base code explicitly cover humanize and underscore for all inputs, which checks R-humanize-unchanged and R-underscore-unchanged, while its camelize/other-function and existing-test-suite parts are extra and require nothing the reference forbids.
